To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the combination of 18 F-FDG and 18 F-FET PET/MRI can be used for non-invasive assessment of treatment responses in patients with NSCLC, and 2) the combination of both PET tracers can be used to identify patients who may benefit from additional treatment.
the use of PET/CT for the evaluation of the response of NSCLC to neoadjuvant chemotherapy is feasible and can be used as a predictor of pathological response.

the addition of FDG-PET to the clinical and radiological staging of patients with NSCLC is associated with a significant improvement in the accuracy of TNM staging, and that the addition of PET to clinical/radiological staging is associated with a statistically significant increase in the proportion of patients who undergo surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a novel PET/CT tracer, 18F-FDG, in the evaluation of the response of non-small cell lung cancers to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
the use of a non-invasive imaging method, 18F-FDG PET/CT, in patients with NSCLC.
the use of PET/CT for the evaluation of patients with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PET-CT is not indicated in all patients with NSCLC.
FDG-PET has a high negative predictive value for the detection of metastases, but its positive predictive value is limited and its role in staging is not yet fully defined.
PET/CT is a useful tool in NSCLC patients with a high NPV for exclusion of N2 disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that FDG PET/CT can be used to predict response and survival after induction therapy in locally advanced non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) and that it may be used as a prognostic marker for patients with stage IIIA NSCLC.
FDG-PET is a useful tool in the management of patients with non-small-cell lung cancer.
we have developed an approach for using FDG-PET imaging to predict pathologic response in NSCLC patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to predict response in a non-invasive way.
the combination of FDG-PET and FDG-PET/CT is useful for predicting the response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with non–small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
the use of FDG-PET/CT in the staging of lung cancer has increased dramatically over the past decade, with a significant increase in the use of FDGPET/CT in patients with stage I lung cancer.
